timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Inchilin and Glucogon. In a previous lesson we learned about hormones and their roles
in regulating and maintaining important processes in our body. In this lesson you will learn
about how your blood glucose level is regulated or controlled by two important hormones,
inchilin and Glucogon via a negative feedback system. When you consume a meal it's
high in carbohydrates such as rice, pasta and bread. This will cause your blood glucose
level to increase. Carbohydrates are essentially long chains of repeating glucose monomer units,
much like beads on a necklace. During digestion this is broken apart into glucose which is absorbed
into our bloodstream. This increased blood glucose level causes a gland known as the pancreas
to create a hormone called insulin. Remember that a gland to create hormones which act on specific
target organs. In this case the target organ is your liver which is stimulated to convert glucose
to glycogen. Glycogen is basically long multi branch chains of glucose monomers stored in
liver and muscle cells. Inchilin also causes your body cells to uptake or take in glucose.
So this decreases your blood glucose level back to its optimal state. When this system is
faulty this leads to a medical condition known as diabetes. If you want to learn more about
diabetes this will be addressed in another video. The same response also occurs when you consume
foods and drinks high in sugar such as sweets, cakes and fizzy drinks. When your blood glucose
level drops such as when you are hungry the pancreas decrease a hormone called Glucogon.
Like insulin the target organ for Glucogon is also the liver though it stimulates the opposite
process the breakdown of glycogon into glucose. This increases your blood glucose level back
to its optimal state. So to review, insulin and Glucogon are two hormones released by the
pancreas which act on the liver to regulate our blood glucose level.
